warning: TEST-ONLY KEYS AND SECRETS. Every secret and private key in this file is public. Never use them outside tests.

source.responses: signed with the gateway's response-signing helpers, pod key 1 and the certificates of v1.json; every signature verdict checked with its reference verifier

model.pin: { vaultId, type: "main"|"test", keys: { ECDSA: xpub|null, EDDSA: xpub|null }, status: "verified"|"unverified", firstSeenAt: Unix seconds, verifiedAt: Unix seconds|null, verification: { rootId, timestamp }|null }
model.configuredPin: { vaultId, type: "main"|"test", keys: { ECDSA: xpub|null, EDDSA: xpub|null } }, at least one xpub, no other field: a pin given in the client configuration (Node pinnedVaultKeys, Python pinned_vault_keys, PHP pinnedVaultKeys), for the client's API origin
model.status: verified: a signed answer (checked against a pinned root) showed these xpubs, or the pin was given in configuration. unverified: only an unsigned answer did, trust on first use; allowed for release candidates while prod does not sign, never reported as verified, and confirmed by the first signed answer that shows the same xpubs.
model.addressCheck: verified (derives from a verified or configured pin) | unverified (derives from an unverified pin) | not_verifiable (a vault without MPC keys, such as SMART, or an address without its derivation path) | mismatch or path_missing, which are errors
model.pathRequired: An address without its derivation path is path_missing, an error, only when all hold: the client's requireAddressPaths is on (Python require_address_paths; its default is the build constant ADDRESS_PATHS_PUBLIC, false while the paths are hidden), the operation is generateDepositAddress, its vault has MPC keys (pinned, or pinned now from the vault lists), and its chain is one the SDK can derive. Lists and addAssetToVaultAccount may answer older rows without a path: not_verifiable.
model.scope: pins are kept per API origin, so test and production pins never mix; these cases are all one origin

rules.order: Verify the answer first (requireResponseSignature false: signed answers must verify, unsigned ones are accepted as unsigned). A refused answer touches no pin.
rules.vaults: Each item of data.items: id, type and the xpub of each algorithm in mpcKeys (algorithm read in uppercase; the first entry of an algorithm counts; algorithms other than ECDSA and EDDSA are ignored). An item without any such key has nothing to pin and is not_verifiable.
rules.outcomes: No pin yet: pinned, verified if the answer was signed, else unverified. Same xpubs as the pin: unchanged, except an unverified pin and a signed answer, which is upgraded to verified. A pinned xpub that differs or is missing: an alarm.
rules.alarm: Any alarm refuses the whole answer: no pin is written or changed, not even for other vaults in it. Each alarm names the vault, the algorithm, the reason (xpub_changed, xpub_missing, xpub_added, type_changed) and the first 16 hex characters of SHA-256 of each xpub (never the xpub itself; null where there is none), ECDSA before EDDSA, then the type, in the order of the answer.
rules.refused: A pinned vault that gains an algorithm it did not have (xpub_added: pinned null, seen the hash of the new xpub) and a vault whose type changes (type_changed: algorithm, pinned and seen null) are alarms like any other: refused, fail closed. The client confirms a legitimate change out of band and re-pins the vault: the command line (npx @vaultody/sdk vault-keys accept) or the store's replace.
rules.configured: A configured pin counts as verified: its vault's status is verified, and an address that derives from it is verified. It is compared with every answer, signed or not, exactly as a stored pin, and any difference is the alarm. It is never written to the store, and the stored pin of the same vault, if any, is neither read nor changed: the configured pin takes its place. Vaults not configured are pinned in the store as usual.

caseFormat.initialPins: the pins in the store before the first step
caseFormat.configuredPins: the pins given in configuration for the whole case (configuredPin); pinsAfter never holds them, and the status of a configured vault is verified
caseFormat.steps: each: the request as sent, the response as received, now, and expected: signature (verified | absent | { error }), outcomes per vault in the order of the answer, or alarms; pinsAfter is every pin after the step, sorted by vaultId
caseFormat.addressChecks: pin status (verified, unverified, configured, or null), whether the vault has MPC keys, whether the address carries its derivation path, the derivation result, and pathRequired when the case is about it ({ requireAddressPaths, operationId, chainKnown }; absent: requireAddressPaths off) → expected status or error
caseFormat.roots: the roots to pin are v1.json keys.roots current and next

cases.name: first_sight_signed
cases.description: A vault seen for the first time in a signed answer is pinned as verified, with the root and the response time as evidence.

cases.name: first_sight_unsigned
cases.description: A vault seen for the first time in an unsigned answer (prod does not sign yet) is pinned as unverified: trust on first use.

cases.name: unverified_confirmed_by_signed
cases.description: An unverified pin is confirmed by a later signed answer with the same xpubs: it becomes verified, and keeps the time it was first seen.

cases.name: unverified_contradicted_by_signed
cases.description: A signed answer shows another xpub than the unverified pin: the alarm. The pin stays as it was and the answer is refused.

cases.name: verified_then_unsigned_same
cases.description: An unsigned answer with the same xpubs leaves a verified pin verified.

cases.name: verified_then_changed_unsigned
cases.description: An unsigned answer with another ECDSA xpub: the alarm.

cases.name: verified_then_changed_signed
cases.description: Even a signed answer never re-pins a changed xpub: the alarm, and only an explicit replace (support, CLI) changes a pin.

cases.name: pinned_algorithm_disappears
cases.description: A pinned algorithm missing from the answer is the alarm too.

cases.name: two_algorithms_changed
cases.description: Both xpubs changed: one alarm entry per algorithm, ECDSA first.

cases.name: alarm_refuses_whole_answer
cases.description: One vault alarms and another is new: the whole answer is refused, so the new vault is not pinned either.

cases.name: smart_vault_not_verifiable
cases.description: A vault without MPC keys (SMART or AUTOMATION) has nothing to pin: not verifiable, never verified.

cases.name: smart_vault_without_mpc_keys_field
cases.description: mpcKeys absent altogether (the field is hidden until the SDK ships): not verifiable as well.

cases.name: other_vaults_untouched
cases.description: A page that does not list a pinned vault leaves its pin as it is: lists are paged.

cases.name: several_vaults_first_sight
cases.description: Several new vaults in one signed answer are all pinned, in the order of the answer.

cases.name: next_root
cases.description: A signed answer certified by the next root pins as verified, with that root as evidence.

cases.name: algorithm_names_case_insensitive
cases.description: mpcKeys algorithm names are read in uppercase, as the API compares them.

cases.name: first_key_of_an_algorithm_wins
cases.description: Two entries for one algorithm: the first counts, as on the server (mpcKeys.find); unknown algorithms are ignored.

cases.name: tampered_signed_answer
cases.description: A signed answer changed on the way (another xpub): refused by the signature check before any pin is looked at.

cases.name: signature_partly_stripped
cases.description: A signed answer with one signature header removed is never treated as unsigned: refused, no pin.

cases.name: pinned_vault_gains_algorithm
cases.description: A pinned vault that gains an algorithm it did not have: refused (xpub_added), fail closed. A legitimate change is confirmed by the client and re-pinned (the command line, or the store's replace).

cases.name: vault_type_changed
cases.description: A vault pinned as a test vault is listed as a main vault: refused (type_changed), fail closed, until the client re-pins it.

cases.name: configured_pin_counts_as_verified
cases.description: A pin given in configuration counts as verified, whether the answer is signed or not: unchanged, and never written to the store.

cases.name: configured_pin_changed_signed
cases.description: A signed answer with another xpub than the configured pin: the alarm, exactly as for a stored pin.

cases.name: configured_pin_changed_unsigned
cases.description: An unsigned answer with another xpub than the configured pin: the alarm as well.

cases.name: configured_pin_gains_algorithm
cases.description: A configured vault that gains an algorithm: refused (xpub_added), as for a stored pin.

cases.name: configured_pin_replaces_stored_pin
cases.description: The configured pin takes the place of the stored pin of the same vault: the answer is compared with the configured xpubs only, and the stored pin is neither read nor changed.

cases.name: configured_and_stored_pins_together
cases.description: Vaults not in the configuration are pinned in the store as usual, next to the configured ones.

cases.name: configured_pin_alarm_refuses_whole_answer
cases.description: A configured vault alarms and another is new: the whole answer is refused, so the new vault is not pinned either.

addressChecks.name: verified_pin_match
addressChecks.description: The address derives from a verified pin.

addressChecks.name: unverified_pin_match
addressChecks.description: The address derives from an unverified (trust on first use) pin: reported as unverified, never verified.

addressChecks.name: smart_vault
addressChecks.description: A vault without MPC keys: not verifiable.

addressChecks.name: no_path_fields
addressChecks.description: An address without accountIndex, isChange and addressIndex (an old row): not verifiable.

addressChecks.name: mismatch_verified
addressChecks.description: The address does not derive from the verified pin: refused.

addressChecks.name: mismatch_unverified
addressChecks.description: Not deriving from an unverified pin is refused just the same.

addressChecks.name: configured_pin_match
addressChecks.description: The address derives from a pin given in configuration: verified.

addressChecks.name: configured_pin_mismatch
addressChecks.description: Not deriving from a configured pin is refused.

addressChecks.name: generate_no_path_required
addressChecks.description: requireAddressPaths on: generateDepositAddress answers an address without its path for a vault with MPC keys, on a chain the SDK can derive: refused.

addressChecks.name: generate_no_path_unverified_pin
addressChecks.description: The same with an unverified pin: refused just the same.

addressChecks.name: generate_no_path_smart_vault
addressChecks.description: requireAddressPaths on, a vault without MPC keys (SMART): nothing to derive, not verifiable.

addressChecks.name: generate_no_path_unknown_chain
addressChecks.description: requireAddressPaths on, a chain the SDK can't derive: not verifiable.

addressChecks.name: list_no_path_required
addressChecks.description: requireAddressPaths on, an address list: its older rows may have no path, so not verifiable.

addressChecks.name: add_asset_no_path_required
addressChecks.description: requireAddressPaths on, addAssetToVaultAccount: it may answer an older address, so not verifiable.

addressChecks.name: generate_no_path_not_required
addressChecks.description: requireAddressPaths off (the default while the paths are hidden): not verifiable.

addressChecks.name: generate_with_path_required
addressChecks.description: requireAddressPaths on and the path given: checked as always.
